**Next steps**

* **Fre
e plan (owner)**: The limit dialog shows **Compare plans** to upgrade, and **Learn more about BYOK** to understand how provider ke
ys and MCPJam credits work separately.\n* **Free plan (admin or member)**: The dialog shows a **Request upgrade** link to email an

n.\n* **Paid plan (member)**: The dialog shows a **Request credits** link to email an organization owner.\n* Add your own API key

zation uses its own keys for all AI features, model tokens are billed by its providers instead; see [Organization AI key policy](#

organization-ai-key-policy).

**Swarm and Eval runs**

When credits run out during a Swarm or Eval run, blocked work stops and
you receive one credit-exhaustion prompt per run, or one per swarm when a swarm launches several runs at once. Completed results
are preserved. Buying credits does not automatically restart the run; start a new run once credits are available.\n\n> [!WARNING]\
n>\n> Bring-your-own-key covers chat. Swarm persona generation and persona-driver\n> turns are billed to MCPJam and have no person
al BYOK path, so adding a key\n> does not lift this limit for a swarm. An organization that uses its own keys\n> for all AI featur
es runs those turns on its default AI model instead, and its\n> providers bill their tokens; see\n> [Organization AI key policy](#

organization-ai-key-policy).

### Credits temporarily held

When it is on, every AI request on the organization's data must ru
n on one of\nthe organization's own providers. MCPJam-provided models, personal keys and\nlocal models are disabled for it, and no
thing falls back to them: a feature\nwithout a compatible provider is unavailable instead. Only direct cloud\nproviders count; Ope

nRouter and local-runtime connections do not.

* **Model pickers** list only the organization's eligible models. A suite's
 ju
dge must be chosen from an organization provider; there is no default\n judge, and a suite without one can't run.\n* **Default AI
model.** Work nobody picks a model for (insights and findings,\n generation, typed decisions, and the simulated user\n in Swarm
and User Testing) runs on the organization's default AI model. An\n admin chooses it under **Organization → AI providers → Defau
lt AI model**,\n and can test it there. MCPJam may suggest one but never sets it. Until it is\n set, that work is unavailable. M
odel pickers never use it, and it is never\n a suite's judge.\n* **Feature coverage** on the settings page shows which features a
re ready,\n and which wait for the default AI model. Features that can't run on\n organization providers yet show **Not supporte
d yet** and are unavailable\n while the setting is on. Today that includes the session map,\n transcription and Ask MCPJam. When
an eligible provider exists, the card\n names choosing the default model as the fix for work that waits on it.\n* **Billing.** M

odel tokens are billed by the organization's providers.
 MCPJam's fixed product fees and usage limits still apply.

Only organ
ization owners and admins can change the setting. Any of them can\nturn it off at any time, including after the organization leave
s Enterprise;\nleaving Enterprise never turns it off. Turning it off is recorded in the audit\nlog, and the organization's owners

get an email.

When a request is refused under the setting, it fails with one of the codes
below.

## Organization provider r

efusals

These codes mean an AI request was refused because it could not run on one of
the organization's own model providers.

None of them count against MCPJam
credits.

Most are configuration: the request won't run until someone changes its model
